item.title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.26695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Marco Vaia, Edoardo Ballini, Alberto Bottarelli, Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke

item.title: Certification of non-stabilizerness in multi-qubit systems via worst-case random access codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.26705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in $m$-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. As an application, we certify magic in $W$ states of arbitrary size using only eight preparations and three single-qubit measurement settings. Motivated by recent work on the stabilizer marginal problem, we then construct prepare-and-measure correlations generated by global $m$-qubit quantum states for which every $k$-qubit marginal lies inside the stabilizer polytope, yet the combined correlations cannot be reproduced by any global stabilizer mixture. Finally, we derive analytical upper and lower bounds on the worst-case bias attainable with mixed stabilizer preparations in an $m$-qubit random access code with $n$ Pauli measurements. For the complete set of $4^m-1$ non-identity Pauli measurements, we show that the optimal quantum and mixed-stabilizer biases both scale as $2^{-3m/2}$, and that their ratio is asymptotically bounded by a constant ($\lesssim 1.85$), showing that in this setting, magic in the preparations alone yields at most a constant-factor advantage over stabilizer mixtures.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Zamora

item.title: Improved Digitization Bounds for U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory via Semiclassical Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.26720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization. Controlling the resulting error is essential for assessing the accuracy and resource requirements of these simulations. In this work, we derive a digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates of the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian for pure U(1) gauge theory and translate it into a bound on time-evolution error. Compared with existing bounds, our result achieves exponentially improved dependence on the inverse lattice spacing $1/a$ and evolution time $T$, together with improved dependence on the inverse coupling $1/g$. The key idea is to identify a small parameter in the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian and apply tools from semiclassical analysis. Specifically, we adapt Agmon's method to establish exponential decay of the error with the truncation threshold. These results sharpen estimates of the local Hilbert space dimension and qubit resources needed to simulate gauge theories near the continuum limit, at weak coupling, and over long times.
item.dc:creator: Di Fang, Yu Tong

item.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.26737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.
item.dc:creator: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

item.title: Efficient Tensor Decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like Potentials and Its Application to Probing Molecular Geometries Using a Quantum Computer
item.description: arXiv:2611.26740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an efficient canonical polyadic decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like potentials in real-space grid representations suited to quantum computing applications. By decomposing the matrix elements of Coulomb-like potentials into low-rank Cartesian components, we achieve $O(N^{1/3})$ T-gate scaling per Coulomb term, where $N$ is the number of grid points (basis functions) per electron, while maintaining high accuracy. This opens a path to significantly reducing the number of basis functions (i.e., qubits) required compared to previous methods by utilizing improved representations of the Coulomb potential that converge faster with grid spacing. The decomposition is also valid for certain pseudopotentials, which can decrease the cost significantly compared to previous work. This efficient decomposition enables the application of block-encoding techniques at larger grid spacings than with previous decompositions, and can therefore be used for algorithms that do not require high energy accuracy. We apply this decomposed Coulomb potential to hydrogen atom energy levels, the helium ground-state energy, and the Hartree-Fock potential energy curve of LiH, and show that modest basis sizes achieve semi-quantitative to quantitative accuracy. As an example of where these faster-converging Coulomb representations can be used on a quantum computer, we discuss their application to probing low-energy molecular geometries, and we estimate the resulting reduction in the cost of real-time evolution.
item.dc:creator: James Brown, Masashi Takahashi, Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield

item.title: Gravity-induced entanglement assisted by an additional interaction using magic angle calibration
item.description: arXiv:2611.26755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravity-induced entanglement provides an operational test of whether gravitational dynamics are compatible with local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but the weakness of the gravitational interaction and the presence of force noise make direct entanglement generation extremely demanding. We introduce a controllable additional coherent interaction that biases two test masses close to, but within, a separability-preservation bound, so that the weak Newtonian coupling supplies only the remaining coherent contribution needed for entanglement. If the additional interaction alone is shown to be incapable of generating entanglement, while entanglement is observed when gravity is included, the gravitational interaction provides a non-LOCC contribution. Since gravity cannot be turned off, we use a magic-angle null of the projected tidal coupling to calibrate the additional interaction and force noise. If the additional dynamics is certified to preserve separability at the magic angle and entanglement is subsequently observed in a non-null configuration, the gravitational contribution is incompatible with an LOCC description within the Markovian model. The protocol trades the stringent absolute force-noise requirement of direct schemes for precision in controlling the additional coupling, its backaction, and angle-dependent systematics.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen

item.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.26762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.
item.dc:creator: Yicheng Song, Zhipeng Yang, Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka

item.title: Frequency-bin-encoded quantum secret sharing with fast basis switching
item.description: arXiv:2611.26816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-bin encoding offers unique opportunities for fiber-native quantum information processing, yet its full potential has been hampered by challenges in rapid state control and protocol scaling. Leveraging high-speed microwave processing, we overcome several extant hurdles and unlock new fundamental capabilities in frequency-based quantum communications. First, we demonstrate three-party quantum secret sharing, representing, to our knowledge, the first multiparty ($N\geq 3$ users) quantum communication protocol implemented entirely with frequency encoding. Second, we demonstrate active, pseudorandom switching of frequency-bin quantum states and measurement bases at 20 MHz symbol rates, enabling real-time protocol operation without relying on hardware-intensive passive basis-selection schemes. Even under fast switching, we preserve high-contrast three-party correlations ($\geq 0.91$) and low quantum bit error rates ($\leq 4.5\%$). Our work extends frequency-bin quantum communication beyond static, two-party protocols, opening a pathway toward scalable, reconfigurable, and real-time spectrally encoded quantum networking.
item.dc:creator: Chen-You Su, Suparna Seshadri, Hsuan-Hao Lu, Jason D. McKinney, Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens

item.title: Scheduling the quantum implementation of the Trotter decomposition for Hamiltonian simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.26884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the quantum computational task for Hamiltonian simulation, the arrangement in which sub-Hamiltonians appear in the Trotter decomposition may have a large influence on the precision, under a given circuit complexity. In this paper, we design several scheduling strategies by combining two methods; that is, the existing simultaneous diagonalization scheme leveraged in order to guarantee the performance in a relatively short circuit depth, with a method inspired from a Trotter-Suzuki decomposition of the second or the fourth order for a better accuracy. By conducting numerical simulations on various Hamiltonian instances, we confirm a systematic advantage over previous methods. Thus, our proposal may eliminate the need of dealing with several Hamiltonian-dependent scheduling strategies.
item.dc:creator: Augustin Ho (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, \'Ecole des Mines de Saint-\'Etienne), Naoki Yamamoto (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, Quantum Computing Center, Keio University)

item.title: Analog Explorations of Quantum State Measurement
item.description: arXiv:2611.26889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The awkward disconnect in the postulates of quantum mechanics between the continuous, deterministic, linear, and unitary evolution governed by Schr\"odinger's equation and the discontinuous, stochastic, nonlinear, and nonunitary measurement process has vexed physicists for decades. Intuition from classical mechanics, statistical mechanics, and dynamical systems theory suggests that such a process might be modeled with a nonlinear system of differential equations. We explore such approaches by designing a deterministic model of an ideal projective measurement on a single qubit and constructing an analog computer that simulates it by manipulating voltages in an electrical circuit. The model reduces to Schr\"odinger evolution when no measurement is taking place. During a measurement, a hidden variable that the observer does not resolve selects the outcome, and the model is constructed so that a uniformly distributed hidden variable yields Born-rule frequencies. We do not derive the Born rule; rather, we show that a deterministic dynamical system with no intrinsic noise can implement it. Over 300 trials, the circuit reproduces the ideal model's individual outcomes to within one percent of the decision threshold, and its outcome frequencies match the Born rule to within about 0.02 in probability. These results are a small but provocative step towards modeling quantum measurement with macro-scale machines---a step of interest for both the foundations of physics and the alternatives to digital computing it suggests.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield

item.title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.
item.dc:creator: Jerry Horgan, Indrakshi Dey, Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper

item.title: Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.26960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, $U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a)$, for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-P\'erot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schr\"odinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition $\delta(\kappa)+\kappa d=n\pi$, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase $\delta$. We also calculate the post-selection probability $P_{RT}$, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor M. Villalba

item.title: Augmenting Quantum Neural Networks with Contractive Layers
item.description: arXiv:2611.27019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical neural networks combine diverse layers with complementary roles to achieve rich expressive capabilities across complex learning tasks. Rapid advances in quantum science and technology have motivated growing interest in their quantum counterparts, quantum neural networks, raising the question of how their expressivity can be enhanced through the design of new quantum layers. Of particular interest are layers that enrich the accessible function space while introducing only a small number of additional trainable parameters. In this Letter, we introduce the contractive layer as a promising building block for quantum neural networks. This layer comprises all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter, enabling efficient control of quantum information flow while maintaining experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays. Using observable learning as a benchmark, we show that contractive layers enhance expressivity more efficiently than simply increasing the depth of conventional brick-wall circuits. This advantage stems from a systematic increase in the accessible target-space dimension per trainable parameter. We further demonstrate similar improvements in image recognition tasks. These results highlight contractive layers as a practical route to expressive quantum neural networks on near-term quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang

item.title: Generalized Wigner-Yanase Uncertainty Bounds for Multiple Quantum Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.27034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive uncertainty relations for quantum channels based on the generalized Wigner-Yanase skew information. For three channels, we obtain a product lower bound by optimizing over permutations of commutator and anticommutator pairings. For an arbitrary number of channels, we establish a lower bound on the sum of squared uncertainties and construct a hierarchy of bounds using the partial Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. These bounds are invariant under changes of Kraus representation for a fixed operator basis. The first two levels of the hierarchy coincide with the elementary arithmetic-geometric mean bound, while the intermediate levels generally depend on the ordering of the operator basis. Examples involving three and four qubit channels demonstrate the bounds and compare their performance with an earlier pairing inequality under fixed channel representations.
item.dc:creator: Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing

item.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
item.description: arXiv:2611.27140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Gaytan, Bradley Lloyd, Paul Kliewer, Chandler Wilburn, Lincoln D. Carr, Adam McCaughan, Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh

item.title: Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of $\kappa_B = 2\kappa_A$, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Ai Zhang, Yan-Zhe Song, Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou

item.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.27251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bu\v{z}ek, Hillery, and Werner.
item.dc:creator: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong

item.title: Pulse-tube-vibration induced Larmor frequency jitter in anisotropic Kramers spins
item.description: arXiv:2611.27267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of pulse-tube mechanical vibrations towards spin frequency noise in a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator. Our system comprises of a low mode-volume superconducting resonator coupled to 50 ppm $\text{Er}^{3+}:\text{CaWO}_4$ spins with highly anisotropic g-factors. By measuring single-shot spin echoes using narrow-bandwidth three-pulse sequences, we directly observe a vibration induced stochastic signal resulting from the spin's Larmor frequency moving into and out of the detection bandwidth. The sensitivity to these vibrations is substantially suppressed when a) the external magnetic field is aligned along the symmetry c-axis and b) spin temperature is modestly increased to 60~mK. We also benchmark the system as a quantum sensor for angular fluctuations, extracting a noise floor of 350 nanodegrees.
item.dc:creator: R. Shaik, P. Kesarwani, S. Rajendran, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan

item.title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.27295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.
item.dc:creator: Tianchun Zhou

item.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.description: arXiv:2611.27300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Ganguly

item.title: Trotter Error Bounds in Lean 4 with a Cancellation-Aware Analysis of the Fourth-Order Suzuki Formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.27359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize the commutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. in Lean 4. For skew-adjoint generators, the local order condition gives an explicit integer step count sufficient to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We apply the theorem in Lean to the binary fourth-order Suzuki formula. For this formula we can also account for cancellation within and between steps. Using local remainder estimates of Casas and Murua, we sum the signed quintic and centered seventh-degree error terms after conjugating each to the interaction picture. For every positive integer step count, we bound the difference between this sum and the global error operator. At fixed time the explicit remainder is eighth order in the step size, and the integral of the conjugated quintic term gives the exact leading error coefficient. The Lean proofs cover the two-generator finite-sum estimates, including the spectral norm for complex matrices. On five ten-site nearest-neighbor Heisenberg instances at time $10$ and tolerance $10^{-3}$, the transported sum meets the tolerance at a mean of $129.4$ steps. Taking a separate norm at each step with the same polynomial and remainder gives a mean first crossing between $184.6$ and $185.2$ steps. The accumulated Casas--Murua local bound at $q=8$ gives a mean of $184.8$ steps.
item.dc:creator: Bingyu Xia, Jue Xu, Yue Wang

item.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.
item.dc:creator: Weijie Du, Filippo Fornetti, James P. Vary

item.title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
item.description: arXiv:2611.27408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schr\"odinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Pouriya Ghadimi, Maximilian Fr\"ohlich, Aaron Sander, Martin Eigel, Richard M. Milbradt

item.title: Explicit construction of the normal cone at every nonlocal extreme behaviour of $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$ and device-independent applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.27413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The set of quantum correlations $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$, in the simplest Bell scenario with two parties performing two binary measurements each, is an object of fundamental interest both in quantum foundations and for device-independent applications. A nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this set can maximize many different Bell expressions, yet these expressions are not all equally useful in a practical experiment. Here, firstly, we give an explicit characterization of every Bell expression maximized by any given nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this Bell scenario. This determines the full normal cone at every such behaviour and makes it possible to optimize over all Bell tests with the same ideal behavior. We then derive an exact variational formula for the quantum bound of an arbitrary Bell expression in this scenario. As an example illustrating the construction, we derive the normal cone for a family of extremal quantum behaviours of importance in device-independent randomness certification, from Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 150403, 2022. Finally, we explore the consequences of this characterization for device-independent randomness generation in practical experiments. Specifically, for any given detection efficiency $\eta \in [0.75,0.98]$, we construct Bell tests and two-qubit experiments that certify more single-round min-entropy from one Bell score than any CHSH score can certify with the same detector efficiency, even when the quantum devices used for the CHSH test are optimized. The results provide a systematic way to choose Bell tests for a desired quantum behaviour and to improve their performance for device-independent applications under experimental imperfections.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Wu, Xie Sicheng, Ravishankar Ramanathan

item.title: The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
item.description: arXiv:2611.27458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbar\omega(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form $\pm i\hbar\omega(z(d/dz)+1/2)$, and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. The two convergence domains correspond to one-sided contraction semigroups of dilations. Finally, we construct bi-coherent states whose biorthogonal position and momentum second cumulants are purely imaginary and complex conjugate, with product $\hbar^2/4$. The corresponding Heisenberg expectation values follow the exact classical hyperbolic trajectories for arbitrary real initial positions and momenta.
item.dc:creator: Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J. -Q. Liang

item.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.27486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though this protective effect diminishes in highly expressive structural settings.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Mondragon-Sampedro, Diego Alvarez-Estevez

item.title: Classical simulability and hardware diagnostics for QAOA on geographic coverage benchmarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-optimization benchmarks can show reduced energy while concealing local loss of weighted covariance. We combine encoding checks with exact structural references to select informative circuit diagnostics for static geographic coverage instances. The executed 24-qubit surrogate has infeasible ground states, whereas a faithful 51-qubit slack encoding preserves its 13 support-graph components and remains exactly simulable blockwise. At the executed angles, the total ideal optimum probability is $5.47\times10^{-20}$, making optimum counts uninformative at the executed budget of $10^5$ shots. A product distribution with the measured bit marginals accounts for about $90\%$ of the observed energy reduction. In three fixed-circuit jobs, the global weighted-covariance ratio is approximately $0.50$, while a five-variable block has ratios between $0.12$ and $0.28$ and contributes only $3.7\%$ of the ideal global denominator. Simultaneous bands resolve its deficit relative to the global ratio under an exploratory conditional counting model. The exact block reference thus reveals a local discrepancy concealed by the aggregate, without identifying an error mechanism or establishing device stability. The procedure links benchmark structure to the resolution and limitations of its observables.
item.dc:creator: F. S. Luiz, D Abreu, A. J. G. Abel\'em, J. E. Da Fonseca, A. F. P. Santos, M. C. de Oliveira

item.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.27523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. The measured Cauchy-Schwarz parameter exceeds unity in both configurations, with a higher central value with filtering ($\overline{R} = 4.15 \pm 0.93$) than without ($\overline{R} = 2.33 \pm 0.20$). This architecture provides actively stabilized rejection of a narrow spectral interval, simultaneously, for two fields detected in different directions. Filter performance could be further improved by adjusting the cavity linewidth to better match the spectral width of the central component and by reducing losses in the filters.
item.dc:creator: G. C. Borges, M. Duclerc, G. Palacios, A. A. C. de Almeida, N. R. de Melo, D. Felinto

item.title: geodesiq: a Python package for geometric diabatic-adiabatic optimal state transfer
item.description: arXiv:2611.27535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the geodesiq Python package, which implements a geometric framework for shaping control pulses that achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems. The underlying method combines adiabatic and diabatic control into a single metric, suppressing unwanted excitations while allowing selected diabatic passages. Finding the pulse thereby reduces to solving a single first-order ordinary differential equation. We explain how to use geodesiq and illustrate its use explicitly with Landau-Zener transitions, spin-qubit initialization, adiabatic many-body ground-state preparation, and a diabatic-adiabatic transfer in a four-level system.
item.dc:creator: David Fern\'andez-Fern\'andez, Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Gloria Platero

item.title: Communication advantages of a quantum switch of two pure-loss channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.27548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum switch can enable communication through otherwise unusable channels, a phenomenon known as causal activation. We show that a switch of two identical pure-loss channels can achieve strictly greater energy-constrained classical and quantum capacities than their sequential use, even when two-way classical communication is available. Remarkably, the switch also activates quantum communication over a range of transmissivities for which the sequential channel has zero quantum capacity.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Marconi

item.title: Block Search Conditioned on Features for Sequential Quantum Data Encoding
item.description: arXiv:2611.27587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential quantum data encoding is addressed through the joint selection of input features and encoding blocks within a fixed quantum register. At each step, a new feature, a block of operations, its placement, and its rotation weights are selected together from training data, extending the incremental construction of Q-FLAIR. With direct-loss selection (RAW), nine to twelve features were retained in four qubits across five new Bars and Stripes datasets. Under the same final calibration, mean changes relative to the calibrated Q-FLAIR reference were +5.53 percentage points in balanced accuracy, -15.83% in binary cross-entropy (BCE), and +7.79% in area under the ROC curve (AUC). The prespecified success criterion was met in four of five datasets and for the mean paired differences. These results were obtained by comparing complete procedures under a common cap of 32 operations.
item.dc:creator: Cec\'ilia S. C. Botelho, Erico S. Teixeira, Anderson F. P. dos Santos, Guilherme D. Lima, Helida Santos, Adenauer Yamin, Renata Reiser, In\^es de Castro Dutra

item.title: Criterion and Construction Framework for Impure Quantum $(r,\delta)$-LRCs from Optimal $(r,\delta)$-LRCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.27626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper aims to uncover new phenomena and provide new tools for quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. The initial motivation is to identify the main reason for the existence of impure cases in such quantum codes. Our main result reveals that whether \(d = r+1\) is the key factor governing the impurity of quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. We prove that, when \(d \neq r+1\), impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs have bounded lengths. Conversely, when \(d = r+1\), we construct impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs with unbounded lengths. The central tool developed in this work is a criterion for identifying impure quantum codes derived from optimal \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs. The main results include a criterion for impurity in quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorem 3.2), a construction framework for impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorem 4.4), and two families of impure quantum \((r,\delta)\)-LRCs (Theorems 4.8 and 4.11).
item.dc:creator: Kun Zhou, Meng Cao

item.title: Quantum control of an electrically levitated nanoparticle with a trapped ion
item.description: arXiv:2611.27634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum control of levitated nanoparticles offers a route towards macroscopic quantum states. Here we propose a novel way to achieve it for a nanoparticle levitated electrically in a linear Paul trap together with a single ion, a system recently realized experimentally. By suitably engineering the trap's AC potential, one can parametrically modulate the ion-nanoparticle distance and thus the Coulomb coupling to enable a resonant interaction. For realistic parameters, we calculate that this enables sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle to its motional ground state by a single, continuously laser-cooled ion. Additional AC drives enable the preparation of squeezed nanoparticle states and of ion-nanoparticle entanglement. Moreover, non-Gaussian states such as Fock and cat states, prepared in the ion with standard trapped-ion techniques, can be transferred to the nanoparticle with high fidelities. We provide complete protocols for each of these states, including all known decoherence sources. Our results establish electrically trapped ion-nanoparticle systems as a platform for quantum control of levitated matter.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Faulend, Dmitry S. Bykov, Tracy E. Northup, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

item.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
item.description: arXiv:2611.27637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.
item.dc:creator: P\'{e}ter Naszvadi, Marcell Tukora, Roman Ku\v{z}el, M\'{a}ty\'{a}s Koniorczyk

item.title: Ancilla-Free Exact Dicke-State Synthesis with Optimal Size and Depth
item.description: arXiv:2611.27640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct exact circuits for $n$-qubit Dicke states of any Hamming weight $k$ using $O(n)$ single-qubit gates and CNOTs in $O(\log n)$ depth without ancillary qubits. The gate count and depth are asymptotically optimal for every $0<k<n$. We compress symmetric blocks to free output qubits for weight-dependent phases. A sign correction followed by a collective rotation produces a state whose overlap with the target is at least a positive constant, so exact amplitude amplification takes $O(1)$ steps. For balanced Dicke states ($k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$), the logarithmic depth disproves the $\Omega(k)$ depth lower bound conjectured by Yuan and Zhang (2025).
item.dc:creator: Yunqi Huang, Wei Zi, Jianhao He, Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng

item.title: Emergent Causality of Macroscopic Transport and Equilibration in Long-Range Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent $\alpha\in(D,D+1)$ in $D$ spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with $\alpha\in (1,3/2)$, whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.
item.dc:creator: Hongchao Li, Marius Lemm

item.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
item.description: arXiv:2611.27660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain Carrozza, Johann Chevrier, Luca Lionni

item.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
item.description: arXiv:2611.27702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.
item.dc:creator: Chia-Ho Ou

item.title: Single-realization Pauli twirling for suppressing coherent error accumulation in structured quantum circuits
item.description: arXiv:2611.27703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pauli twirling is conventionally understood as an ensemble-level noise-tailoring procedure which suppresses coherent components of the error channel by averaging over randomized compilations. This picture does not by itself determine whether a single realization of Pauli-dressed circuit can outperform its bare counterpart, nor does it predict when such an advantage should occur. In this work, we present single-realization based framework for the standard Pauli dressing of two-qubit Clifford gates in structured quantum circuits. This is afforded by the key insight that for weak coherent errors, the leading gate infidelity is governed by the variance of some accumulated error generator. Through both simulations and theoretical considerations, we verify that coherent errors accumulated at different entangling gates can produce $\Theta(L^2)$ variance growth in a bare circuit, whereas independent Pauli dressing eliminates the cross-layer contribution on average and yields an $O(L)$ variance bound at any fixed confidence level for a single randomly sampled realization. We then develop a covariance diagnostic that predicts when this mechanism is effective in error mitigation. We find a strong Pauli twirling advantage for coherent errors whose transported generators have large off-diagonal covariance, and little advantage when the covariance matrix is nearly diagonal. Hardware experiments on IBM superconducting processors demonstrate fidelity improvements for GHZ-state preparation and reduced observable errors in Trotterized transverse-field Ising dynamics. These results indicate that single realizations of Pauli twirling without ensemble averaging is a useful coherent-error suppression technique for structured circuits containing repeated nontrivial two-qubit operations.
item.dc:creator: Dihang Sun, Tianqi Chen, Jin Ming Koh, Nannan Ma, Jiangbin Gong

item.title: Beyond the Stabilizer Norm: Physicality and Resource Allocation in Pauli-Limited Quantum Certification
item.description: arXiv:2611.27724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Certification from restricted and uncertain Pauli measurements can be posed as a robust optimization problem: among all physical channels consistent with the data, how small can the fidelity with a target channel be? We first study a linear relaxation that ignores positivity and show that it is exactly characterized by a single scalar, the stabilizer norm of the target Choi state, $s_{\mathrm{wit}}(U)=\|C_U\|_{\mathrm{st}}-1/D$. We then ask whether this scalar continues to determine robustness once the positivity constraint is restored. It does not. We derive a necessary and sufficient KKT condition for the relaxation to remain tight, together with a dual obstruction certifying a strict gap, and give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that two distinct two-qubit targets can have exactly the same stabilizer norm but different physical robustness. The KKT condition depends on structure discarded by the stabilizer norm, including the support and relative signs of the Choi-Pauli coefficients and the algebraic relations among the corresponding Pauli operators. We use this structure to derive simpler sufficient certificates for a strict gap. The dual coefficients also determine how measurement uncertainty enters the finite-data fidelity bound. For a fixed budget, we derive exact shot-allocation rules for a fixed certificate and for compatible observables obtained from shared measurement settings, and we formulate the corresponding joint certificate-design problem. The conjecture that every full-support two-qubit target has positive gain remains open.
item.dc:creator: Shreya Savadatti, Peter Yun Zhang

item.title: Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.27769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. Of the many consequences of this lack of conditional expectation, we consider the problem of defining the quantum conditional relative entropy, i.e., the relative entropy between two quantum states conditioned to a sub-region or sub-algebra. We discuss how, when the conditional expectation map is not defined, there are multiple, non-equivalent ways to define a quantum conditional relative entropy quantity, and we present some of their properties. Classical conditional relative entropy has played a fundamental role in many applications to spin systems, and in particular in proving logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. A key feature of conditional relative entropy that intervenes in these results is its quasi-factorization or approximate tensorization property: informally, the relative entropy is almost super-additive over weakly-dependent sub-algebras. It is then not surprising that the key to obtaining similar applications in the quantum setting, such as quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities in spin systems, has been to obtain approximate factorization results for the quantum conditional relative entropy, with the added complication that there is not a unique definition of conditional relative entropy to work with. We review the recent results regarding quasi-factorization of the quantum conditional relative entropy, in strong and weak forms.
item.dc:creator: Angelo Lucia, \'Angela Capel

item.title: Complex chaotic Boltzmann machines as deterministic representations of quantum states
item.description: arXiv:2611.27779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural networks and tensor networks have opened new ways to explore quantum systems by parameterizing families of wave functions through the structure and parameters of a network. Here we extend this perspective to a dynamical representation: we introduce a complex chaotic Boltzmann machine that assigns a deterministic system to a pure quantum state. We extend Suzuki's construction to incorporate both Born probabilities and relative phases. The probabilities set the trajectory velocities in a hypercube, while the phases define a complex field that lifts its Poincare sections. The evolution is determined by the network parameters and initial conditions, without random choices during flights or configuration changes. Our analysis of two qubits and study of three-qubit families show how relations between probabilities organize regular curves, islands, and unstable regions, and how phases distinguish states that share the same Born dynamics. This architecture turns a wave-function parameterization into a geometry of trajectories, providing a tool to explore probabilities, phases, and symmetries together across families of states.
item.dc:creator: J. Montes

item.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
item.description: arXiv:2611.27787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.
item.dc:creator: Chia-Ho Ou

item.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.27815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without $\textit{a priori}$ specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.
item.dc:creator: Kasidit Srimahajariyapong, Thiparat Chotibut, Suwannachad Suwannajitt, Tithivich Paka, Ricard Puig, Yudai Suzuki, Marek Gluza, Zo\"e Holmes, Supanut Thanasilp

item.title: Tackling Many-Body Coulomb Singularity by Randomization
item.description: arXiv:2611.27851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many-body Coulomb dynamics is central to quantum chemistry and molecular simulation, yet the Coulomb singularity undermines both the standard error analysis and performance of product formulas. Even for the simple hydrogen ground state, the celebrated Trotter formulas converge more slowly than their nominal order, and going to higher order does not help. Randomization by itself does not resolve this. We show that conventional qDRIFT suffers the same loss of accuracy, and that for general initial states, the errors of both Trotter formulas and qDRIFT can decrease more slowly than any power of the number of time steps (logarithmically). To overcome these limitations, we introduce supersmoothing qDRIFT, a randomized product formula that turns a physical property of free particle propagation into an algorithmic resource. Our algorithm achieves an error bound that decreases linearly with the time step, uniformly over \textit{all} initial states and without any smoothness or energy assumptions. Combined with spatial discretization analysis, the resulting end-to-end gate count improves on those of qubitization and high-order Trotter formulas applied directly to the discretized Hamiltonian, despite first-order convergence in time. This work demonstrates new ways of utilizing continuum dynamics to achieve algorithmic advantage.
item.dc:creator: Di Fang, Wook Yoon

item.title: World Models for Learning Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose using world models for learning Hamiltonians from measured dynamics of a quantum computer or simulator. Implicitly, the parameters of a Hamiltonian are encoded in how the measured few-body observables evolve. By using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to perform prediction in latent space, we show that the device Hamiltonian can be efficiently inferred from noisy measurements. We train a spatiotemporal encoder and predictor with approximately $2.7$ million trainable weights using a single objective, to predict the representation of the next window of measurements from the previous one. The network is thereby driven to retain the reproducible dynamics and discard shot noise. We recover the field and coupling maps of a two-dimensional Ising lattice in real and imaginary time, and the disorder map of a one-dimensional Heisenberg chain of $100$ sites. In every settings the encoder achieves lower error than a masked autoencoder and than the same encoder left untrained. It also outperforms the same regression head applied directly to time-averaged observables, by factors of $4.4$ to $30$. We establish latent prediction as a practical self-supervised objective for learning from measurements of quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Wang, Oleksandr Kyriienko

item.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.
item.dc:creator: Marko Male\v{z}i\v{c}, Johann Ostmeyer

item.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2611.27914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.
item.dc:creator: Aryan Gadhave, Asghar Ghorbanpour, Liam Hickey, Masoud Khalkhali, Allison Klingler, Nathan Pagliaroli, Andrew Parks

item.title: Transpilation-Aware Multi-Vendor QPU Scheduling with Predicted Post-Transpilation Fidelity
item.description: arXiv:2611.27927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cluster schedulers already choose nodes, GPUs and accelerators for submitted workloads, enforce quotas and spread load. QPUs from several vendors are now schedulable resources in the same clusters, yet the user still names the device, usually the one with the best average fidelity. For a given circuit that choice is often wrong: compiling onto each device's qubit connectivity adds gates, so a job can meet its required success probability on one device and miss it on another with similar error rates, and checking this exactly by compiling for every candidate is too slow for a scheduling decision. We let the scheduler choose the QPU in two stages. A training-free estimate predicts, in milliseconds and without compiling, the success probability on every candidate and filters out those that would miss the requirement; only the chosen device then compiles the circuit, re-checks it, and binds the job or rolls back. The estimate matches compiling every candidate at about 25x lower latency in simulation, ranks measured success on IBM hardware as well as the post-compilation estimate (Spearman rho = 0.95), reduces requirement violations from tens of jobs to a few, and avoids them under contention without piling jobs onto one device. Across vendors it works when error rates are comparable (IBM and IQM) and fails when published figures overstate a device.
item.dc:creator: Ana Paula Appel

item.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
item.description: arXiv:2611.27942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.
item.dc:creator: David Rosser

item.title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.27975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Zin, Andrzej Veitia

item.title: Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
item.description: arXiv:2611.26071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $\gamma$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $\gamma$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.
item.dc:creator: A. Leviatan

item.title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.26659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Maleki

item.title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.26693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Shen Lee, Itamar Kimchi

item.title: Cavity-Controlled Hysteresis and Multilevel Molecular Switching in Hybrid Optomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.26724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate cavity-controlled hysteresis and multilevel molecular switching in a hybrid molecular optomechanical system composed of a plasmonic nanocavity, a Fabry-P\'erot cavity, and an ensemble of molecular vibrations. Molecular-plasmonic optomechanical interaction together with cavity-plasmon hybridization produce bistability and dynamical hysteresis, leading to a history-dependent optical and molecular response. An analytical treatment of the steady-state equations shows that the auxiliary cavity renormalizes the effective optical linewidth and detuning, while the collective molecular interaction generates an effective nonlinearity.
