Together, these effects enable control of the hysteretic regime through optical detuning, cavity-plasmon coupling, and molecular ensemble size. Beyond bistability, pulsed excitation generates staircase-like molecular dynamics, with ascending or descending vibrational populations depending on the optical driving configuration. In particular, the FP cavity controls the buildup of vibrational excitation, while simultaneous driving of both optical modes enables stepwise vibrational depletion. These results establish hybrid molecular optomechanical systems as a tunable platform for history-dependent and pulse-driven molecular dynamics, with potential applications in nanoscale memory, multilevel information processing, and optically controlled molecular switching.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Molinares, Ra\'ul Coto, Vitalie Eremeev, Eduardo Chamorro

item.title: Quantum-Chaos-Assisted Measure Synchronization in a Double-Well Ultracold Bose Gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.27256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates measure synchronization (MS) in a two-component ultracold atomic system confined in a double-well potential, which realizes a quantum many-body bosonic Josephson junction. Through spectral-statistics analysis, we identify the quantum chaotic parameter regime and confirm that the system achieves MS within this regime with weak dependence on the initial energy imbalance. We further show that chaotic dynamics not only significantly shortens the time scale for establishing synchronization but is also accompanied by entanglement entropy approaching the random-state prediction. These results reveal close connections among quantum chaos, MS, and quantum entanglement in conservative quantum many-body systems and may motivate further studies on the underlying mechanisms of chaos-assisted synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Xianchao Le, Jiaxin Peng, Weiping Zhang, Keye Zhang

item.title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.27328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. The cavity uses a rigid Zerodur spacer to suppress the negative effects of thermal drift and mechanical-acoustic vibrations on the atomic motional state. The 60 cm-long cavity spacer provides ample optical access for the laser beams and imaging optics necessary for the preparation, quantum control, and read-out of the atomic state, as well as room for various source mass configurations for localized gravitational measurements. An integrated differential pumping structure enables compatibility with ultrahigh-vacuum operation and optical interferometry allows for in-situ vibration monitoring. The performance of the optical cavity is methodically characterized: we measure mirror vibration noise with amplitude below 5 nm/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ in a wide frequency range of 2 Hz - 100 kHz and a slow 15 MHz thermal drift of the cavity resonance over 47 hours, which can be readily stabilized with an integrated piezo. The optical cavity supports both 852-nm light for Raman transitions and 1064-nm light for the optical lattice, with a free spectral range matched to an integer divisor of the cesium ground-state hyperfine splitting.
item.dc:creator: Philip Wondrak, Paola Luna, Kenneth Nakasone, Andrei Zhukov, Michael Grisham, Garrett D. Cole, Po-han Chen, Cristian D. Panda

item.title: Reset Quantum Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.27417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Argoud, Alain Joye

item.title: Diameter Growth of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ under Cliff Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cliff metrics are right invariant Riemannian metrics on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ introduced by Nielsen and his collaborators in the geometric approach for gate complexity in quantum computations. In this paper, we compute the exponential growth rate for the diameter of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ equipped with cliff metrics as $N \rightarrow \infty$. We prove that if the norm of most generalized Pauli matrices are sufficiently large, this growth rate coincides with the growth rate of maximal gate complexity obtained by Knill.
item.dc:creator: Xiaobo Liu, Lei Zheng

item.title: Bayesian Quantum Thermometry of Ultracold Gases with Non-Equilibrium Single-Atom Probes
item.description: arXiv:2611.27584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Precise thermometry is essential for experiments with ultracold quantum gases, but conventional techniques such as time-of-flight thermometry are destructive and lose sensitivity at low atomic densities. Quantum probes provide an alternative route by encoding temperature information in accessible internal degrees of freedom. Here, we implement Bayesian thermometry with non-equilibrium spin-based single-atom probes immersed in an ultracold atomic bath. Temperature-dependent spin-exchange collisions map the bath temperature onto the internal spin populations of the probe atoms. Measurements of these populations are then used to iteratively update a Bayesian temperature estimate. We connect the information gained at different measurement settings to the underlying spin dynamics, identifying intersections of temperature-dependent population trajectories as a source of thermometric ambiguity. Using the expected information gain to optimize measurement settings, we experimentally compare unoptimized, a priori optimized, and adaptively optimized protocols. Both optimized protocols accelerate convergence, with the adaptive protocol reducing the average number of measurements required to reach a prescribed precision by a factor of 2.5 compared with the unoptimized protocol. In the many-measurement regime, we further characterize the protocols through their asymptotic error scaling and the accumulation of Fisher information, while testing consistency with the expected Cram\'er-Rao bound (ECRB) and the Bernstein-von Mises theorem. These results connect the microscopic dynamics of a quantum probe to efficient measurement design and establish Bayesian spin thermometry as a practical approach for ultracold-gas experiments.
item.dc:creator: Julian Fe{\ss}, Luca Granert, Sabrina Burgardt, Silvia Hiebel, Alexander Guthmann, Mohammad Mehboudi, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet, Artur Widera

item.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
item.description: arXiv:2611.27600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetry breaking does not occur when the same systems are modified to display $PT$ symmetry instead. Our findings highlight contrasting behaviors in time-dependent and time-independent non-Hermitian systems, creating new possibilities and opportunities for future investigations.
item.dc:creator: Li Ge

item.title: Quantum-Informed Regularized Poisson Learning for Graph-Based Semi-Supervised Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.27609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce IPQSSL, a quantum-informed regularized Poisson framework for graph-based semi-supervised classification under scarce labels. Local graph feature contexts are QR factorized, lifted to unitary encodings, and processed by a shared variational circuit whose measurements yield node wise diagonal weights that stabilize a symmetrized Poisson system. We establish positive definiteness of the symmetrized, regularized operator under explicit spectral conditions and derive a Hermitian, block encoding compatible formulation that separates the classical NISQ oriented implementation from a future fault-tolerant pathway. Across seven benchmarks spanning tabular data and a citation network, the effect of regularization is dataset- and budget-dependent: IPQSSL improves over the Poisson baselines on Iris and Wine at all but the single-label budget, reaching 0.946 accuracy on Iris at ten labels per class and at every budget on German Credit, where, however, all methods remain below the majority class rate. Original Poisson remains preferable on Breast Cancer, Heart Disease, Optdigits, and Cora, with the deficit narrowing as the label budget grows on the two largest graphs. Ablations attribute the gains to diagonal stabilization rather than variational training. The result is a resource transparent bridge between Poisson graph learning and quantum linear algebra, with an explicit empirical delineation of when diagonal regularization helps.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Gholipour, Farid Bozorgnia, Hamzeh Mohammadigheymasi, Joao Neves, Moharram Challenger

item.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.27623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.
item.dc:creator: Roman Ku\v{z}el, M\'aty\'as Koniorczyk, Janez Povh

item.title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
item.description: arXiv:2611.27632v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking. Research also rarely examines how such pedagogical choices unfold across the undergraduate-to-graduate trajectory. Using textbooks as an analytical lens to map these choices and characterize overarching pathways, encompassing entry points and overall orientations, we comparatively analyze the selection, sequencing, and contextualization of core topics across these 3 dimensions, alongside prefaces and introductions, in 36 university QM textbooks spanning countries and eras. At the topic level, we show that identical topics occupy widely different curricular roles depending on their contextualization. Synthesizing these findings into pathways, we identify three additional entry-point archetypes (labeled path-, qubit-, and axiom-first) and characterize all 5 approaches, showing that most textbooks combine multiple archetypes in their opening chapters. Extending this synthesis beyond entry points, we map textbooks' overall orientations relative to mathematics, experiment and application, and theoretical physics. Interpreting these profiles alongside authors' rationales reveals how educators navigate competing trade-offs among mathematical accessibility, theoretical generality, physical motivation, and modern developments. This study provides a multidimensional framework, substantive examples, and a practical roadmap for textbook selection and curriculum design in QM education.
item.dc:creator: Yajie Liang, Menno Poot, Carsten Schuck, Stefan Heusler

item.title: Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally
item.description: arXiv:2611.27707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. This allows us to use one-body transport results to establish the expected many-body transport behavior on finite time scales in the following two illustrative settings: (i) We prove quantum diffusion, as quantified by a certain operator spreading diagnostic, in weakly interacting and weakly disordered Fermi systems in dimensions $D\geq2$ on large finite time scales based on the non-interacting diffusion result of Black, Drogin, and Hern\'andez [arXiv:2506.06468]. (ii) We show for Fermi-Hubbard models with initially low spin-down density, that all local multi-time spin-up correlation functions are approximated by their free counterparts. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].
item.dc:creator: Jorge Acu\~na Flores, Joscha Henheik, Marius Lemm, Daniele Toniolo

item.title: Pseudo-entropy in Thouless Pumps and Majorana Topological Phases
item.description: arXiv:2611.27846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the average excess pseudo entropy, $\Delta S_{12}$, in the Rice-Mele model under Thouless pumping. We compute it for two driving schemes, the control-freak and smooth pumps, under open and periodic boundary conditions. We find that $\Delta S_{12}$ distinguishes the trivial, monomer, and topological stages of the pump, and that it depends on the boundary condition, the driving scheme, and the reference time. We also find that a nonzero staggered potential breaks chiral symmetry and gaps out the SSH critical point, thereby flattening the pseudo-entropy peak at the phase boundary. We also study reference-state dependence in the open Kitaev chain, comparing a fixed even-parity target with five reference families: even free-fermion, pairing-only, vacuum, and two fixed gapped states. We find that the pseudo-entropy response depends on the reference and on the parity of the subsystem size, even when the reference remains gapped. At $\mu=0$, the pairing-only reference gives the exact result $S_{\mathrm{pr}}=\ln 2$ for $L=4m+2$, while the $L=4m$ sequence has analytically determined finite-size corrections. These results show that, in both models, pseudo entropy is a property of the reference-target pair and the subsystem partition, rather than a reference-independent signature of the topological phase.
item.dc:creator: Nabaraj Khatri, Shuvam Chudal, Ashish Khanal

item.title: Quantum Dobrushin comparison and locality of fermionic equilibrium states
item.description: arXiv:2611.27873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a quantum analogue of Dobrushin's comparison theorem for lattice fermions. As in the classical case, it is a tool for proving uniqueness of equilibrium states, decay of correlations, and stability of local expectations under distant perturbations. We apply it to fermions with weak many-body interactions added to a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing pairing, spatial inhomogeneity and long-range interactions. If the quadratic Hamiltonian is gapped, there is a coupling strength below which the thermal equilibrium (KMS) state is unique at every positive temperature and its correlations decay uniformly in the temperature. Its local expectations converge to those of the unique gapped ground state exponentially fast in the inverse temperature. In the same regime, local perturbations perturb locally in a strong sense (strong LPPL): every equilibrium state of a system with a distant defect is locally close to the equilibrium state without the defect, however strong or extended the defect is. The same holds for finite-volume Gibbs states with arbitrary even boundary terms. Without a gap, uniqueness, decay of correlations and strong LPPL hold at each positive temperature for interactions below a coupling strength that depends on the temperature. At high temperature, they hold for general interactions.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Becker, Harman Preet Singh, Stefan Teufel

item.title: Thermo-electric Response Bound on Fluctuations in Coherent Transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.27884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an accessible lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport, expressed in terms of responses to reservoir temperatures and chemical potentials. Derived within the Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism using a Cram\'er-Rao-type inequality, it holds for arbitrary linear combinations of charge and heat currents in normal terminals, including those of hybrid superconducting systems, under static or periodic driving. The bound is tight in experimentally relevant regimes, notably in quantum point contacts with static or oscillating voltages and normal-superconductor junctions, often providing stronger constraints than thermodynamic uncertainty relations. It can be evaluated via experimentally accessible response coefficients, without inferring entropy production or dynamical activity, and provides useful constraints on the precision of nanoscale thermal and quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Gianmichele Blasi, Rosa L\'opez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Sungguen Ryu

item.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
item.description: arXiv:2611.27982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Chakraborty, Dario Rosa

item.title: Logical qubits with geometrically enhanced energetic and parametric protection
item.description: arXiv:2405.08138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Breaking the error-threshold marks a milestone in establishing quantum advantage for a wide range of relevant problems. One possible route is to encode information redundantly in a logical qubit by combining several noisy qubits, providing an increased robustness against external perturbations. We propose a setup for a logical qubit in a generalized Tavis-Cummings model consisting of physical qubits coupled to a logical all-to-one element. Our design is based on a recently discovered geometric stabilizing mechanism in the closely related Bose-Hubbard wheel, which manifests as energetically well-separated clusters of many-body eigenstates. We show that even in the presence of typical fabrication uncertainties, their occurrence and separation is extremely robust. Introducing an additional physical qubit coupled to the central element yields replicas of these clusters, for which we introduce two prototypical coupling schemes. (i) A local coupling protocol exploits the spectral separation to encode information redundantly. (ii) A non-local coupling protocol additionally generates a symmetry-protected operating point at which virtual transitions produce no leading-order differential energy shift within the logical manifold. Our results establish geometrically stabilized many-body spectral clusters as tools to construct logical qubit manifolds with independently tunable energetic and parametric error protection.
item.dc:creator: Reja H. Wilke, Leonard W. Pingen, Thomas K\"ohler, Sebastian Paeckel

item.title: Slow Mixing of Quantum Gibbs Samplers
item.description: arXiv:2411.04300v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Preparing thermal (Gibbs) states is a common task in physics and computer science. Recent algorithms mimic cooling via system-bath coupling, where the cost is determined by mixing time, akin to classical Metropolis-like algorithms. However, few methods exist to demonstrate slow mixing in quantum systems, unlike the well-established classical tools for systems like the Ising model and constraint satisfaction problems. We present a quantum generalization of these tools through a generic bottleneck lemma that implies slow mixing in quantum systems. This lemma focuses on quantum measures of distance, analogous to the classical Hamming distance but rooted in uniquely quantum principles and quantified either through Bohr spectrum jumps or operator locality. Using our bottleneck lemma, we establish unconditional lower bounds on the mixing times of Gibbs samplers for several families of Hamiltonians at low temperatures. For classical Hamiltonians with mixing time lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n^\alpha)]$, we prove that quantum Gibbs samplers also have $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n^\alpha)]$. This applies to models like random $K$-SAT instances and spin glasses. For stabilizer Hamiltonians, we provide a concise proof of exponential lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n)]$ on mixing times of good $n$-qubit stabilizer codes at low constant temperature. Finally, we consider constant-degree classical Hamiltonians and show how to lift classical slow mixing results in the presence of a transverse field using Poisson Feynman-Kac techniques. We show generic results for models with linear free energy barriers, and we demonstrate that our techniques extend to models with sublinear free energy barriers by proving $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[n^{1/2-o(1)}]$ for the ferromagnetic 2D transverse field Ising model.
item.dc:creator: David Gamarnik, Bobak T. Kiani, Alexander Zlokapa

item.title: Quantum state transfer of superposed multi-photon states via phonon-induced dynamic resonance in an optomechanical system
item.description: arXiv:2501.01647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a method to transfer macroscopically superposed states between two optical cavities mediated by a mechanical oscillator, which works in a nonlinear regime of optomechanical interaction. The scheme relies on phonon-induced dynamic resonance, where the motion of the mechanical oscillator dynamically sets on/off the resonance between the two cavities. It assumes the high-amplitude limit of the oscillator, weak coupling between optical cavities, and the adiabatic approximation. We show that, under these conditions, various multi-photon quantum states, especially Schr{\"o}dinger cat states, can be faithfully transferred in a deterministic process. Our approach thus suggests the possibility of transferring large-photon-number quantum states, beyond the few-photon regime typically accessible with linearized optomechanical interactions.
item.dc:creator: Xuanloc Leu, Xuan-Hoai Thi Nguyen, Jinhyoung Lee

item.title: Mitigating transients in flux-control signals in a superconducting quantum processor
item.description: arXiv:2503.08645v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Flux-tunable qubits and couplers are common components in superconducting quantum processors. However, dynamically controlling these elements via current pulses poses challenges due to distortions and transients in the propagating signals. In particular, long-time transients can persist, adversely affecting subsequent qubit control operations. We model the flux control line as a first-order RC circuit and introduce a class of pulses designed to mitigate long-time transients. We theoretically demonstrate the robustness of these pulses against parameter mischaracterization and provide experimental evidence of their effectiveness in mitigating transients when applied to a flux-tunable qubit coupler. The proposed pulse design offers a practical solution for mitigating long-time transients, enabling efficient and reliable experiment tune-ups without requiring detailed flux line characterization.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Aggarwal, Jorge Fern\'andez-Pend\'as, Tahereh Abad, Daryoush Shiri, Halld\'or Jakobsson, Marcus Rommel, Andreas Nylander, Emil Hogedal, Amr Osman, Janka Bizn\'arov\'a, Robert Rehammar, Michele Faucci Giannelli, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, Jonas Bylander, Giovanna Tancredi

item.title: The Locality of Quantum Theory Does Not Require Complex Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2504.02808v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Complex numbers are central to the standard formulation of quantum theory, but whether they are fundamentally necessary remains unsettled. Familiar real formulations reproduce quantum predictions but fail to be representation-local: local physical operations need not correspond to local entities in the mathematical representation. Here we show that representation-local formulations based solely on real numbers nevertheless exist. Our construction is based on the observation that not every structural feature of finite-dimensional density-matrix quantum theory over the complex numbers need be retained in a real formulation. Specifically, we reconsider two features inherited from the complex formalism: the use of the Kronecker product as the system-combination rule and the representation of states and effects by positive semidefinite matrices. Relaxing only one of these assumptions at a time, we first obtain a representation-local real quantum theory with a modified combination rule that closely parallels the conventional complex formulation. We then show that even with the usual Kronecker-product rule a representation-local real formulation exists, provided states and effects are not required to be positive.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'ee Hoffreumon, Mischa P. Woods

item.title: Adaptive Entanglement Distillation
item.description: arXiv:2504.11670v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum network applications impose a variety of requirements on entanglement resources in terms of rate, fidelity, latency, and more. The repeaters in the quantum network must combine good methods for entanglement generation, effective entanglement distillation, and smart routing protocols to satisfy these application requirements. In this work, we focus on entanglement distillation in a linear chain of quantum repeaters. While conventional approaches reuse the same distillation scheme over multiple hop lengths after entanglement swaps, we propose a novel adaptive quantum error correction (QEC) scheme that boosts end-to-end metrics. Specifically, depending on the network operating point, we adapt the code used in distillation over successive rounds to monotonically increase the rate while also improving fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy using three codes, with parameters [[9,1,3]], [[9,2,3]], [[9,3,3]], and a new performance metric, efficiency, that incorporates both overall rate and fidelity. Since the minimum input fidelity for QEC-based distillation is high, we then extend our study to include non-QEC-based purification protocols, specifically DEJMPS since it outperforms others. We compare the performance of end-to-end DEJMPS against adapting from DEJMPS to QEC once DEJMPS improves the initial fidelity to the threshold for QEC. Through a refined efficiency metric, we illuminate the regime where QEC is beneficial. These results provide a detailed outlook for entanglement purification and distillation in first and second generation quantum repeaters.
item.dc:creator: Sijie Cheng, Narayanan Rengaswamy

item.title: Interpreting quantum reference frame transformations through a simple example
item.description: arXiv:2508.09540v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum reference frame transformations have been proposed to provide a means by which to translate descriptions of quantum systems relative to each other. At present, there are several differing frameworks for describing quantum reference frames, with concomitantly different transformation rules. Here, we investigate a simple example of three qubit systems with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry in order to analyze physical and conceptual distinctions between three contemporary approaches to quantum reference frames -- dubbed perspective-neutral, extra particle and operational. By constructing two three-qubit states that are indistinguishable by observables relative to one frame but are distinguishable by observables relative to another, we show that each of the three approaches provides a distinct transformation rule, which may be understood to reflect differing attitudes towards the global state and the information that can be accessed by each frame. This helps us to shed light on the operational meaning of each approach and the contexts in which they may be most naturally applied.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Castro-Ruiz, Thomas D. Galley, Leon Loveridge

item.title: A Rigorous Quantum Framework for Inequality-Constrained and Multi-Objective Binary Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2510.13983v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Encoding objectives into Hamiltonians forms the foundation of quantum optimization. Including inequality constraints into these encodings remains a major challenge. In this work, we show that including inequality constraints is equivalent to having multiple objectives. This insight motivates the Multi-Objective Quantum Approximation (MOQA) framework, which comes with rigorous performance guarantees. MOQA operates directly at the Hamiltonian level and is compatible with ground state solvers such as quantum annealing or the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA).
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Egginger, Alexander Mandl, Kristina Kirova, Sonja Bruckner, Stefan Hillmich, Richard Kueng

item.title: Local quantum coherence with intersource interactions at nonzero temperature
item.description: arXiv:2511.04242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local quantum coherence in a two-level system (TLS) is typically generated via time-dependent driving. However, it can also emerge autonomously from symmetry-breaking interactions between the TLS and its surrounding environment at a low temperature. Although such environments often consist of interacting atoms or spins, the role of interactions within the environment in generating the autonomous local coherence has remained unexplored. Here, we address this gap by analyzing an exactly solvable model, which comprises a target TLS coupled to $N$ interacting source TLSs that represent the environment, with the whole system being in thermal equilibrium. We show that the local coherence not only persists but can be enhanced at finite temperatures of the environment compared to the case of no intersource interactions. The temperature dependence of the coherence bears signatures of a ground-state level crossing, and our analytical results suggest strategies for its optimization. Our findings reveal generic properties of the autonomously generated quantum coherence and point to viable routes for observing the coherence at nonzero temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Yehor Hudenko, Michal Kol\'a\v{r}, Radim Filip, Artem Ryabov

item.title: In defense of temporal Tsirelson bound
item.description: arXiv:2512.24304v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent paper, Chatterjee et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett 135, 220202 (2025)] analyze and experimentally implement a specific unitary evolution of a simple quantum system. The authors refer to this type of dynamics as a "superposition of unitary time evolutions." They claim that such an evolution enables a violation of the temporal Tsirelson bound in the Leggett-Garg scenario, a claim that is supported by their experimental results. In this work, we show that the proposed evolution can be understood within a more conventional framework, without invoking a superposition of evolutions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the apparent violation of the bound arises because the measured quantities are not consistent with the necessary conditions for the temporal Tsirelson bound.
item.dc:creator: Antoni W\'ojcik, Jan W\'ojcik

item.title: Efficient Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Long-time Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.18756v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurately simulating long-time dynamics of many-body systems is a challenge in both classical and quantum computing due to the accumulation of Trotter errors. While low-order Trotter-Suzuki decompositions are straightforward to implement, their rapidly growing error limits access to long-time observables. We present a framework for constructing efficient high-order Trotter-Suzuki schemes by identifying their structure and directly optimizing their parameters over a high-dimensional space. This method enables the discovery of new schemes with significantly improved efficiency compared to traditional constructions, such as those by Suzuki and Yoshida. Based on the theoretical efficiency and practical performance, we recommend two novel highly efficient schemes at $4^{\textrm{th}}$ and $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of these decompositions on the Heisenberg model and the quantum harmonic oscillator, and find that for a fixed final time they perform better across the computational cost. Even when using large time steps, they surpass established low-order schemes like the Leapfrog. Finally, we investigate the in-practice performance of different Trotter schemes and find the decompositions with more uniform coefficients tend to feature improved error accumulation over long times. We have included this observation into our choice of recommended schemes.
item.dc:creator: Marko Male\v{z}i\v{c}, Johann Ostmeyer

item.title: RF-free control of nuclear spins with color centers in silicon carbide
item.description: arXiv:2601.21499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Color centers that enable nuclear-spin control offer a powerful route towards simplified and scalable quantum devices. Such capabilities are especially valuable for quantum sensing and computing platforms that already find applications in biology, materials science, and geophysics. A key challenge is the coherent manipulation of nearby nuclear spins, which serve as quantum memories and auxiliary qubits but conventionally require additional high-power RF fields which increase the experimental complexity and overall power consumption. Finding systems where both electron and nuclear spins can be controlled using a single MW source is therefore highly desirable. Here, using a modified divacancy center in silicon carbide, we show that coherent control of a coupled nuclear spin is possible without any RF fields. Instead, MW pulses driving the electron spin also manipulate the nuclear spin through hyperfine-enhanced effects, activated by a precisely tilted external magnetic field. We demonstrate high-fidelity nuclear-spin control, achieving 89% two-qubit tomography fidelity and nearly T1-limited nuclear coherence times. This approach offers a simplified and scalable route for future quantum applications.
item.dc:creator: Raphael W\"ornle, Jonathan K\"orber, Timo Steidl, Georgy V. Astakhov, Durga B. R. Dasari, Florian Kaiser, Vadim Vorobyov, J\"org Wrachtrup

item.title: Loss-insensitive reduction of amplified quantum noise in a Raman amplifier with coherent feedback
item.description: arXiv:2602.22567v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A quantum amplifier usually adds extra noise inevitably through coupling to internal degrees of freedom while amplifying the signal. The introduction of quantum correlations can effectively suppress this extra noise. In this work, we utilize the established quantum correlation between the Stokes field and atomic spin waves in the Raman amplification process to feed back a portion of the Stokes field into the amplifier. This leads to a reduction in amplified quantum noise that is independent of the feedback loss at high gain. A maximum of 6 dB noise reduction is observed. The single-path feedback amplifier is found to be sensitive to the feedback phase due to quantum interference, and we experimentally demonstrate an improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio of $4.4\pm 0.7$dB for a phase signal encoded in the feedback loop compared to the case without feedback. This general concept can be extended to integrated optics and fiber-optic systems with potential applications in quantum precision measurement.
item.dc:creator: Jianmin Wang, Rong Zhu, Z. Y. Ou

item.title: Interferometrically Enhanced Asymmetry in Strong-field Ionization with Bright Squeezed Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2604.12646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that quantum light statistics can be used to control strong-field ionization at the tunneling step leaving the average driving field unchanged. Using a bichromatic linearly polarized field composed of a strong coherent driver and a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV), we show through simulation that the asymmetry of the resulting photoelectron momentum distributions is significantly enhanced, with the skewness increasing by roughly two orders of magnitude compared with an equally weak coherent perturbation. A semiclassical analysis based on the strong-field approximation (SFA) reveals that the effect originates from asymmetric fluctuations in the instantaneous field amplitude, which strongly modify the tunneling ionization probability while leaving the electron's continuum dynamics essentially unchanged. The resulting amplification provides a proof of concept for enhancing phase-sensitive signatures of sub-cycle ionization dynamics.
item.dc:creator: G. Singh, T. Rook, J. Rivera-Dean, C. Figueira de Morisson Faria

item.title: General framework for anticoncentration and linear cross-entropy benchmarking in photonic quantum advantage experiments
item.description: arXiv:2604.15258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Photonic architectures are one of the leading platforms for demonstrating quantum computational advantage, with Boson Sampling and Gaussian Boson Sampling as the primary schemes. Yet, we lack for these photonic primitives a systematic theoretical understanding of linear cross-entropy benchmarking (LXEB), which is a central tool for testing quantum advantage proposals. In this work, we develop a representation-theoretic framework for the classical computation of average LXEB scores and second moments of output probability distributions, covering a range of quantum advantage experiments based on scattering $n$-photon states through $m$-mode Haar-random interferometers. Our methods apply in any regime, including the saturated regime, where the (expected) number of photons is comparable to the number of optical modes. The same second-moment techniques also allow us to prove anticoncentration for traditional Fock-state Boson Sampling in the saturated regime. Interestingly, for Gaussian Boson Sampling second moments are not sufficient to establish a meaningful anticoncentration statement. The technical core of our approach rests on decomposing two copies of the $n$-particle bosonic space $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^m)$ into irreducible representations of $\mathrm{U}(m)$. This reduces two-copy Haar averages to computing purities of initial states after partial traces over particles, highlighting the role that particle entanglement plays for LXEB and anticoncentration.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an Kolarovszki, \'Agoston Kaposi, Zolt\'an Zimbor\'as, Micha{\l} Oszmaniec

item.title: Contracting Tensor Networks with Generalized Belief Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2604.24760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent years have seen a growing interest in the use of belief propagation (BP), an algorithm originally introduced for performing classical statistical inference on graphical models, for approximate, but highly efficient tensor network contraction. BP is a corner case of generalized belief propagation (GBP), a family of classical inference methods in which messages are passed within a hierarchy of overlapping regions. Here, we detail how to apply GBP to tensor network contraction. We implement GBP with different region choices on finite and infinite tensor networks in two and three dimensions, solving the corresponding fixed point equations numerically and, in tractable cases, analytically. We consider a range of quantum and classical examples, including frustrated Ising models, three-dimensional ice models, independent-set counting on irregular graphs, and the norms of the deformed AKLT state and random tensor network states. Across our examples, including the quantum ones, converged GBP often reduces errors by several orders of magnitude compared with BP.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Tindall, Grace M. Sommers, Hilbert Kappen

item.title: Capacity of multimode quantum Gaussian channels
item.description: arXiv:2605.19749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive explicit formulas for the capacity of multimode quantum Gaussian channels which serve as a fundamental model for optical version of multiple-input multiple-output channels. We show that it is always optimal to increase the number of modes under fixed power constraint. We derive an analytical formula for the ensemble-averaged Holevo capacity in the case of random passive transformations. The analogous results are also obtained for capacities achievable under homodyne and heterodyne detection. We further discuss the generalization of the model to include weak active transformations.
item.dc:creator: Maria Pop{\l}awska, Marcin Jarzyna

item.title: An interpretable closed form for entanglement entropy from bitstrings, guided by a graph neural network
item.description: arXiv:2606.22713v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The empirical bitstring distribution is the most accessible observable on Rydberg-atom arrays, but the bipartite von Neumann entropy it constrains is far costlier to obtain. We present a six-term linear closed form for the entropy, built from bitstring features whose choice is guided by a trained graph neural network (GNN). Probing the GNN shows that its entropy prediction is routed through the atom pairs that straddle the bipartition boundary, so we compute the two-point correlators over these pairs only. An exhaustive search scored against exact entropies then selects the form. The form is human-readable but less accurate than the GNN in distribution, where its mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.024 nats is 6.4 times larger. Fit once and applied unchanged, however, it has lower MAE than the base GNN on five of six out-of-distribution pools and ties it on the sixth. Refit per Hamiltonian family, it reaches 29-70 millinats (mnat) on the four sign-definite families we tested. Further out of distribution, we test it on density-matrix renormalisation group ground states of up to one hundred atoms. There the slopes must be refit per size, which gives a cross-validated MAE of 15-37 mnat, and size laws fitted to the slopes without the target size give 24-95 mnat with no labels at that size.
item.dc:creator: Anas Saleh

item.title: Spin-Momentum Impedance and Filtering at a Spin-Coupled Absorbing Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2606.25650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a separable harmonic waveguide, transverse confinement leaves the longitudinal bulk Hamiltonian unchanged. Earlier simulations nevertheless found that stronger confinement suppresses prompt detection of a spin-1/2 particle at a spin-coupled absorbing boundary. Here we identify the local boundary response underlying this effect. We treat the boundary as an effective detector, identifying the squared-norm loss rate with the detection-time probability density. The incident transverse ground state has a distribution of momenta parallel to the detecting plane, with characteristic scale proportional to $\sqrt{\omega}$, where $\omega$ is the confinement frequency. For each parallel momentum, we resolve the boundary relation into two spin channels. At fixed normal wave number and detector parameter, local matching gives these channels equal absorption probabilities but generally different reflection phases. Their common absorption probability decreases with the magnitude of the parallel momentum. Simulations over several observation windows distinguish reduced detection probability from changes in recorded-click timing. The mean detection time capped at horizon $T$ is summarized by the empirical fit $A_T+B_T\sqrt{\omega}$ over the sampled range, with setup- and horizon-dependent coefficients. The local response makes detection sensitive to transverse confinement; propagation, interference, and repeated encounters of the undetected wave shape the detection-time distribution.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Jozani

item.title: Quantum Convolutional Autoencoders for Reconstruction-Based Anomaly Detection
item.description: arXiv:2607.02135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) are increasingly used in quantum machine learning (QML) due to their efficient parameterization and hierarchical representation of quantum information. Anomaly detection has important applications across many domains, including scientific data analysis. In this work, we adapt a QCNN architecture into a quantum autoencoder (QAE) framework for semi-supervised, reconstruction-based anomaly detection. The models are trained on normal samples to reconstruct feature-extracted and dimensionally reduced time-series data, with reconstruction error used as an anomaly score. We investigate two quantum convolutional autoencoder architectures that differ in their treatment of latent information: a hierarchical architecture in which information remains distributed across the circuit and a bottleneck-based architecture in which information is explicitly compressed and reconstructed using additional decoder qubits. The latent-space size is varied to study its influence on reconstruction and anomaly-detection performance. The approaches are benchmarked against a variational quantum circuit and classical baselines using the Kepler exoplanet dataset and pulsar candidates from the High Time Resolution Universe Survey (HTRU-2). The models are evaluated over ten deterministic optimization seeds at matched four- and eight-component input dimensions and matched latent-space sizes where feasible. Across all available compressed matched configurations, the bottleneck QAE achieves higher ROC AUC than the hierarchical QAE, with all differences remaining significant after Holm correction. The preferred compressed latent-space size depends on the dataset and architecture. The strongest classical autoencoder performs better than both quantum autoencoder families on HTRU-2, while the supervised neural network achieves the strongest overall discrimination on both datasets.
item.dc:creator: Donovan Slabbert, Francesco Petruccione

item.title: Analysis of polarization drift of optical signals over deployed aerial-inground fiber connections
item.description: arXiv:2607.07629v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polarization measurements of a classical 1550-nm signal are collected and analyzed on 15-km hybrid aerial-inground fiber connections over 11 months. The spectral area and spectral moments of mHz-resolution Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) of these measurements are extracted, and related to temperature, humidity, wind speed, and time of day. Spectral area correlations show a strong diurnal structure: daytime maxima align with temperatures/wind speed peaks and humidity dips, with lower levels during the night. These diurnal patterns also show seasonality, with higher mean and variance in summer than winter. A random forest regressor is used to estimate FFT features from environmental measurements, informed by a theoretical model.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Aneesh Ramaswamy, Nageswara S. V. Rao, Joseph C. Chapman, and Muneer Alshowkan, "Analysis of polarization drift of optical signals over deployed aerial-inground fiber connections," Opt. Express 34, 42428-42440 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Aneesh Ramaswamy, Nageswara S. V. Rao, Joseph C. Chapman, Muneer Alshowkan

item.title: Nonlinear Optics Mediated by Chiral Waveguide QED: Generation of Momentum-anticorrelated Photon Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2607.18562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In recent years, chiral quantum optics has emerged as an active research area due to the promising applications in quantum information processing as well as nonlinear optics. In this work, we present results on the properties of the incoherent component of the transmitted light after transmons chirally coupled to a waveguide. The well-known resonance fluorescence of one chiral transmon resembles nonlinear quantum optics as it can convert the coherent light, with photons having spatially extensive coherence and Poisson distribution, into a field with spatially localized coherence and bunching photon statistics. However, another chiral transmon can undo the effect of the first transmon regardless of the Rabi frequency under the idealization involved in this work. A full wavefunction calculation shows that, in the weak driving limit, this incoherent light mainly comes from two-photon processes - one chiral transmon converts two independent photons into a momentum-correlated photon pair. In addition to the driving through the waveguide, we study the role of a local drive with independently tunable amplitude and phase that can address each transmon individually. The interplay between the waveguide and local driving modulates the contribution of the incoherent transmission and hence enables the engineering of the quantum statistics of the transmitted field, with tunable $g^{(2)}(0)$ spanning anti-bunched, coherent, and strongly-bunched regimes.
item.dc:creator: Wenqi Tong, Spencer J Walsh, H. Alaeian, F. Robicheaux

item.title: An Analytically Trained Variational Quantum Circuit using the Output Probability Distribution of Quantum Phase Estimation on NISQ Hardware
item.description: arXiv:2607.20943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE) is the standard algorithm for molecular ground-state energy estimation and often serves as a subroutine in larger quantum algorithms, but its deep circuits make it impractical on current noisy hardware. A previous variational approach replaces the QPE subroutine with a shallow Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) trained to reproduce the QPE measurement distribution, but generates the training target by classically simulating the full QPE circuit, which is prohibitive for molecules. We reformulate this idea, computing the training target analytically from the Dirichlet kernel, using only a reference energy, the number of ancilla qubits and the evolution time, so the controlled-unitary and inverse-QFT operations of QPE are never simulated. Using H$_2$, we select the VQC stepwise by comparing its IBM Quantum hardware output with the target using four metrics. We first choose the entangler (linear or full) and number of layers of an $R_Y$-$R_Z$-$CZ$ ansatz, with and without dynamical decoupling (DD). As DD degraded performance with depth, we then choose, without DD, the ansatz ($R_Y$-$R_Z$-$CZ$ or $R_Y$-$CZ$) and the training simulator (ideal or noisy). The configuration fixed on H$_2$, a single-layer linear-entangler $R_Y$-$CZ$ ansatz trained on the ideal simulator, is validated on LiH, H$_2$O, BeH$_2$, NH$_3$, CH$_4$, O$_2$ and N$_2$, recovering the dominant QPE bitstring on hardware with errors within chemical accuracy ($1.59 \times 10^{-3}$ Ha) for all eight molecules at the chosen evolution times. We also analyze the hardware side lobes of both ans\"atze, and a noise analysis of the selected ansatz at 8 and 64 layers examines how DD performs with depth. As training requires a known reference energy, the surrogate is not meant for standalone energy estimation, but can replace the QPE subroutine where a larger algorithm uses only its measurement outcome.
item.dc:creator: Mousumi Kundu, Ashish Kumar Patra, Anurag K. S. V., Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Alok Shukla, Jaiganesh G

item.title: Thermal Quantum Correlations in Coupled Andreev Spin Qubits with Tunable Superconducting Phase and Spin Orbit Interaction
item.description: arXiv:2607.24521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate thermal quantum correlations in two coupled superconducting spin qubits described by an effective Andreev spin-qubit Hamiltonian with spin-orbit interaction. Using Local Quantum Fisher Information (LQFI) and Local Quantum Uncertainty (LQU), we examine the effects of superconducting phase difference, tunneling amplitude, spin-orbit coupling, and temperature. Our results show that quantum correlations decrease with increasing temperature but are enhanced by stronger tunneling and spin-orbit interaction. The superconducting phase induces periodic variations in the correlations through its modulation of the effective exchange couplings. We further demonstrate that larger energy gaps between the ground and first excited states suppress thermal excitations and enhance the stability of quantum correlations. A comparison with negativity reveals the distinct behaviors of these correlation measures, while LQFI is consistently greater than or equal to LQU in the investigated parameter regime. These findings clarify the mechanisms governing thermal quantum correlations and highlight the roles of phase engineering, spin-orbit interaction, and tunneling in protecting quantum resources in superconducting hybrid systems.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Reza Pourkarimi, Mina Shiri, Mehdi Monemi, Vadim Ohanyan

item.title: Better accuracy with fewer qubits: Single-particle basis set optimization for quantum chemistry on quantum computers
item.description: arXiv:2608.02119v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In spite of recent advances, quantum computers are expected to be sufficiently noisy in the coming few years to the extent of limiting quantum chemical calculations to relatively small number of orbitals. However, even with reasonable quality single particle basis sets, small active spaces with limited orbitals can result in a significant fraction of correlation energy being lost, motivating the design of moderate quality qubit-efficient basis sets for quantum algorithms. We begin by reoptimizing the existing minimal basis sets using a genetic algorithm-inspired approach in conjunction with aggressive refinement strategies, and generate modified minimal basis sets (MSTO-kG basis; k = 2-11) for atoms from H through F. The ground state energies of H through F using our MSTO bases at FCI level of theory yield ground state energies that are comparable or sometimes even lower than those obtained using 6-31G basis sets. In the case of Li, the MSTO bases surpass the performance of cc-pVQZ bases. Thus, we obtain better atomic energies with same number of qubits relative to STO bases, and better/comparable energies with fewer qubits relative to higher quality bases. In the case of molecules, H2 performs poorly; a finding that is consistent with an earlier work in literature. For other molecules, Li2, C2, LiH, BeH and BeH2, the FCI results (except C2 for which we employ CISD) from our bases are comparable to/outperform those from 6-31G basis. Finally, we compare the resources required between different bases and find that MSTO bases yield better energies than the competing basis sets while incurring fewer qubits and two-qubit gates with VQE, QPE, and HHL. The logical T-gate counts are also found to be considerably lower for QPE and HHL respectively. Overall, our work paves way for more accurate yet less qubit-hungry quantum chemical calculations using near-term quantum computers.
item.dc:creator: Subimal Deb, V. S. Prasannaa

item.title: Entanglement and non-local magic in a non-unitarily deformed non-Hermitian bipartite system
item.description: arXiv:2608.08346v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-Hermitian degeneracies are usually discussed through spectral coalescence, whereas entanglement is a property of eigenvectors and need not be fixed by the eigenvalues alone. We formulate a compact bipartite model that separates these two notions. A Hermitian operator with a degenerate eigenspace is transformed by an invertible non-unitary similarity map. The resulting Hamiltonian is non-Hermitian and retains a non-defective degeneracy at every finite value of the non-Hermiticity parameter. For an exactly solvable two-qubit realization, the right eigenstates evolve continuously from product states to maximally entangled states although the spectrum is unchanged. We distinguish the positive right-state reduced density matrix from the generally non-positive biorthogonal reduction, for which entropy may become complex. The same two-qubit solution gives a closed partial-transpose negativity and a Schmidt-gauged non-local magic. Entanglement grows monotonically with the non-Hermiticity parameter, whereas the non-local magic vanishes for both the product and maximally entangled limits and is largest at an intermediate coupling. In larger bipartite spaces, the Page entropy and Haar-averaged purity provide reference values for eigenstate typicality. These diagnostics separate non-defective degeneracy, exceptional-point sensitivity, Haar-typical entanglement, and non-stabilizer correlations without relying on a proliferation of basis-dependent spectral quantities.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Huan Wu

item.title: Geometric signatures of the onset of many-body ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2608.14818v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Identifying universal, robust, and interpretable signatures of the onset of many-body quantum ergodicity remains a major challenge. The adiabatic gauge potential has been noted to act as a sensitive probe of quantum chaos. Here, we generalize the features of the adiabatic gauge potential to multi-parameter perturbations, yielding an emergent quantum geometry. This new geometry --- whose metric we dub the Hilbert-Killing metric --- provides a tool for probing the onset of ergodicity. The Hilbert-Killing metric exhibits a quantifiable fastest growth in the boundary regime, which we corroborate by exact diagonalization of the mixed-field Ising chain and the disordered PXP chain.
item.dc:creator: Chris Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, Francisco Machado, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ

item.title: A State-of-the-art Squeezed-Light Source for Hybrid Quantum Photonics: Current Performance and Remaining Challenges
item.description: arXiv:2608.18950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hybrid quantum photonics seeks to combine the complementary advantages of continuous- and discrete-variable quantum optics. This typically entails photon-counting measurements on entangled states generated by interfering many single-mode squeezed-vacuum (SMSV) states. However, because conventional photon-counting schemes are mode-insensitive, it is critical that the SMSV states occupy a single, well-defined mode. Achieving this requires careful engineering of the process, which determines both the spatial and spectro-temporal properties of the generated state. In addition, the ideal source must be massively scalable, capable of efficiently generating strong squeezing, and remain compatible with existing detection schemes and fiber networks. Although many platforms address one or more of these requirements, satisfying all of them simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we present a source that simultaneously addresses all of these requirements: a single-pass, periodically poled, Type-II potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) waveguide optimized for scalable hybrid quantum-photonic architectures. The SMSV state produced by the source has a measured effective mode number of 1.24. Furthermore, the source is extremely bright (producing up to 40 000 photons per pulse) and operates at a central wavelength of 1546nm, optimized for fiber-network compatibility and which, in combination with picosecond duration, also enables intrinsic photon-number resolution in superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Although this source constitutes an ideal source in a simplified picture, the ultimate limitations of any source will be governed by complex dynamics that arise when the system is driven at high-gain or due to unavoidable loss during state generation. We have therefore developed a complete theoretical framework that enables a comprehensive photon-counting-based characterization...
item.dc:creator: Kai-Hong Luo, Denis Kopylov, Florian L\"utkewitte, Jan-Lucas Eickmann, Simone Atzeni, Fabian Schlue, Benjamin Brecht, Torsten Meier, Polina Sharapova, Michael Stefszky, Christine Silberhorn

item.title: Auditing Encoder Reseeding for Quantum Error Correction under a Bounded Cloud Fault Model
item.description: arXiv:2608.26600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for large-scale quantum computation due to the inherent noise in physical qubits, which renders them unsuitable for algorithm execution. This issue poses a security risk for shared cloud processors, where faults may be introduced by adversaries rather than random noise. Given that the same code is used for every execution, an adversary who identifies an undetected fault can exploit it in all subsequent executions. This study evaluates whether per-run reseeding, which involves encoding each execution with a new random circuit derived from the seed, can prevent such replay attacks. We examine two types of cloud adversaries: the provider, who compiles the circuit and thus knows the seed, and a co-tenant, who shares the processor but selects faults without seed knowledge. To address this, we define accepted corruption as the logical alteration caused by a fault in executions that the verifier accepts. We also derive the expected accepted corruption over Haar-random encoders in closed form; this expectation is exact for uniform Clifford encoders, thereby quantifying the threat posed by any fault chosen without seed knowledge. Our findings indicate that seed-blind reseeding reduces the proportion of executions corrupted by a replayed fault under both adversaries to a rate that decreases exponentially.
item.dc:creator: Ziqing Guo, Anthony Lawrence, Renyu Wang, Randy Kuang, Ziwen Pan

item.title: Fractal dimension predicts quantum kernel collapse in angle-encoded data
item.description: arXiv:2609.00475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Angle-encoded quantum kernels on tabular data collapse when the feature map is wider than the intrinsic dimension of the data. We propose the correlation fractal dimension D2 as an a priori qubit budget: encode D2 coordinates chosen by FD-ASE instead of the PCA-95% width or all E attributes. On nine data sets and a statevector simulator (n= 32), a one-layer ZZ fidelity kernel at q=D2 stays geometrically alive while the same kernel at the PCA-95% width has already collapsed. The budget is map-dependent: product-state and IQP maps overshoot it; a second ZZ layer undershoots it. Packed dense-angle and re-uploading encodings still live at the fractal q, but not when PCA-95% features are stacked onto those qubits. Shrinking the angle bandwidth moves the ZZ knee later; stretching it kills the kernel earlier. On IBM Quantum (ibm_fez, 256 shots, n=8) the one-layer ZZ kernel at the fractal width matches the exact kernel (MAE 0.021); past that width both hardware and simulator have collapsed. The ceiling is a property of the map-data pair at a stated bandwidth, not of the classical table alone.
item.dc:creator: Ana Paula Appel

item.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
item.description: arXiv:2609.12527v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Laux, Eric G. Cavalcanti

item.title: The effects of shot noise on the quantum computation of NMR spectra
item.description: arXiv:2609.20406v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in the field of quantum computing hardware motivate the search for applications which demonstrate so-called quantum advantage. One promising use case that has been identified is the simulation of quantum many-body systems. The computational resources required for performing such a simulation on a classical computer generally grow exponentially with the size of the system being modeled, which is ultimately due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space in which the dynamics of such a system take place. While digital quantum computers natively evolve quantum states directly in such a Hilbert space, thus naively avoiding this problem, the result of such a computation is typically not obtained as a deterministic output. Rather, it requires projective measurements which are fundamentally affected by shot noise. Any desired expectation values must therefore be reconstructed from repeated measurements, making the number of those measurements a relevant computational resource, and thus an important consideration for any potential claims of quantum advantage. In this work, we study how this resource scales with system size (a scaling which itself depends on the desired accuracy of the final result), using the simulation of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra as a test case. We study this scaling for both real-world molecules, as well as a class of model NMR Hamiltonians which allow for efficient large-scale simulations with one-dimensional, two-dimensional, and all-to-all interactions. We find that the required resources increase only weakly with molecular size, far below the exponential growth of the underlying Hilbert space. This result suggests that shot noise should not pose a fundamental barrier to achieving quantum advantage in the simulation of NMR systems, and perhaps for many-body systems more broadly.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Walch, Keith R. Fratus, Jan-Michael Reiner, Igor Lesanovsky

item.title: Quantum Encoding Agents: A Natural Language Interface for Data Embedding Strategy Selection in Quantum Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2609.31902v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Selecting a data encoding is a central and poorly tooled decision in quantum machine learning. The feature map fixes the geometry of the Hilbert space, the expressibility of quantum kernels, and whether the circuit can run on near-term hardware. This paper presents Quantum Encoding Agents, an open-source system that turns encoding selection into a natural-language interaction. Given a dataset and an optional task description, it profiles the data, applies a hardware-aware policy using the gate-error threshold p* approximately 10^{-3}, returns a copyable Qiskit circuit with a justification in Portuguese or English, and scores the quantum kernel by Kernel-Target Alignment (KTA). When a numerical matrix is available, it estimates the correlation fractal dimension D_2 and selects original columns with FD-ASE, using q* = max(2, ceil(D_2)) as a qubit budget so that angle and IQP maps are not proposed at a width where the fidelity kernel has collapsed. The service implements seven encoding families: amplitude, angle, dense angle, IQP, basis, data re-uploading, and custom feature map. On benchmark datasets, KTA separates these encodings under realistic NISQ constraints.
item.dc:creator: Ana Paula Appel

item.title: Materialised symmetries of 2D translationally invariant codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.06036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There has been significant recent interest in near-term qLDPC codes as high-performance alternatives to surface and color codes. One such class of codes is 2-dimensional translationally invariant (TI) codes, such as bivariate bicycle codes, which share similar properties to topological codes. Fundamental objects in the study of such codes are the materialised symmetries, which can be used for the construction of matching-based decoders. These decoders generalise the minimum-weight perfect matching decoder for toric codes and provide similar asymptotic performance guarantees that heuristic decoders such as BP and its variants lack. Despite this, the mathematical structure of symmetries along with their properties under translation and restriction to finite-sized lattices has not been well-studied. We describe a decomposition of symmetry spaces of 2D CSS TI codes on infinite lattices into translation-invariant subspaces which allow us to write an explicit basis of symmetries in a plane-wave-like form. We then describe how to adapt this infinite lattice basis so that any corresponding rectangular periodic lattice basis can be obtained by restriction to basis elements compatible with the periodic boundaries. This allows us to describe how the symmetry space varies with different rectangular dimensions. We illustrate via examples that it is often straightforward in practice to determine a basis of symmetries on twisted boundaries as well, without needing to recompute the decomposition. We comment on the applications of this framework to matching-based decoders and provide examples of symmetries of such codes as the gross code.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Li, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, Campbell K. McLauchlan

item.title: Semiclassical dynamics of higher-order squeezing: self-adjoint extensions and coherent returns
item.description: arXiv:2610.33378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.
item.dc:creator: A. E. Teretenkov

item.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34176v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $\theta$ and $\eta$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $\theta$ and $\eta$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
item.dc:creator: Pinaki Patra

item.title: A Unified Protocol for Arbitrary Z Rotations of a Class of Bosonic cQED Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2610.36754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bosonic-qubit encodings provide diverse approaches to storing and processing quantum information, with logical operations often implemented through encoding-specific physical strategies. Here, we identify a class of bosonic Fock-based qubits in circuit QED for which distinct implementations of arbitrary $Z(\theta)$ rotations share a common structure. The applicability of the proposed framework is determined by specific conditions involving the greatest common divisor of the photon numbers and a parity criterion for the logical codewords. These conditions provide a systematic means of identifying bosonic Fock-based cQED qubits that admit the common implementation.
item.dc:creator: Vahid Shaghaghi

item.title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
item.description: arXiv:2610.39091v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.
item.dc:creator: Nizar Khalfet, Francisco A. Monteiro, Ioannis Krikidis

item.title: Entangled Measurement Outcomes for Optimal Postselection in Quantum Batteries
